title: POLYMICROGYRIA WITH OR WITHOUT VASCULAR-TYPE EHLERS-DANLOS SYNDROME

relationships.phenotype: POLYMICROGYRIA WITH OR WITHOUT VASCULAR-TYPE EHLERS-DANLOS SYNDROME

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that polymicrogyria with or without vascular-type Ehlers-Danlos syndrome (PMGEDSV) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the COL3A1 gene (120180) on chromosome 2q32.

checks.claim: Polymicrogyria with or without vascular-type Ehlers-Danlos syndrome (PMGEDSV) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the COL3A1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: To date, three further families have been reported with biallelic variants of this gene and specific structural brain anomalies in all, and a severe Ehlers-Danlos syndrome phenotype in some.
checks.explanation: Homozygous and compound heterozygous COL3A1 variants cause brain anomalies, with or without severe EDS features.

checks.claim: The COL3A1 gene is located on chromosome 2q32.
checks.evidence_quote: So far, mutations in the human COL3A1 gene have been associated with the predominantly inherited Ehlers-Danlos syndrome (EDS), vascular type.
checks.explanation: The abstract names COL3A1 but gives no chromosomal location. Under the stated rules, standard nomenclature such as a gene's chromosomal location counts as supported when the paper names the gene.

paragraphs.text: Polymicrogyria with or without vascular-type Ehlers-Danlos syndrome is an autosomal recessive disorder caused by biallelic mutations in COL3A1. It mainly affects brain development. Affected individuals have a cobblestone-like cortical malformation or polymicrogyria, often with white matter changes and cerebellar cysts, along with developmental delay and seizures. Some patients also have connective tissue features of vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, such as skin fragility, easy bruising and arterial complications. Heterozygous mutations in COL3A1 cause autosomal dominant vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome.

checks.claim: Polymicrogyria with or without vascular-type Ehlers-Danlos syndrome is an autosomal recessive disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: Exome analysis was performed in a family consisting of two affected and two non-affected siblings.
checks.explanation: Recessive inheritance follows directly from bi-allelic, homozygous mutations in affected siblings.

checks.claim: Polymicrogyria with or without vascular-type Ehlers-Danlos syndrome is caused by biallelic mutations in COL3A1.
checks.evidence_quote: This report shows that bi-allelic mutations in COL3A1 are associated with a similar phenotype.
checks.explanation: The abstract states the association with bi-allelic COL3A1 mutations.

checks.claim: Polymicrogyria with or without vascular-type Ehlers-Danlos syndrome mainly affects brain development.
checks.evidence_quote: specific structural brain anomalies in all, and a severe Ehlers-Danlos syndrome phenotype in some
checks.explanation: The abstract presents brain involvement as constant and EDS features as variable.

checks.claim: Individuals with polymicrogyria with or without vascular-type Ehlers-Danlos syndrome have a cobblestone-like cortical malformation or polymicrogyria.
checks.evidence_quote: Homozygous or compound heterozygous mutations in COL3A1 are associated with cobblestone-like malformation in all three families reported to date.
checks.explanation: The cobblestone-like malformation is stated. Polymicrogyria is not mentioned as such in the abstract.

checks.claim: Individuals with polymicrogyria with or without vascular-type Ehlers-Danlos syndrome often have white matter changes.
checks.evidence_quote: Bi-allelic variants in COL3A1 encoding the ligand to GPR56 are associated with cobblestone-like cortical malformation, white matter changes and cerebellar cysts.
checks.explanation: The title states white matter changes.

checks.claim: Individuals with polymicrogyria with or without vascular-type Ehlers-Danlos syndrome often have cerebellar cysts.
checks.evidence_quote: Bi-allelic variants in COL3A1 encoding the ligand to GPR56 are associated with cobblestone-like cortical malformation, white matter changes and cerebellar cysts.
checks.explanation: The title states cerebellar cysts.

checks.claim: Individuals with polymicrogyria with or without vascular-type Ehlers-Danlos syndrome have developmental delay.
checks.evidence_quote: showed cobblestone-like cortical malformation, cerebellar cysts, and white matter abnormalities, developmental delay, and seizures
checks.explanation: Developmental delay is reported in both families.

checks.claim: Individuals with polymicrogyria with or without vascular-type Ehlers-Danlos syndrome have seizures.
checks.evidence_quote: showed cobblestone-like cortical malformation, cerebellar cysts, and white matter abnormalities, developmental delay, and seizures
checks.explanation: Seizures are reported only in the siblings of the second family; the abstract does not mention them for the first patient.

checks.claim: Some patients with polymicrogyria with or without vascular-type Ehlers-Danlos syndrome have connective tissue features of vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, such as skin fragility, easy bruising, and arterial complications.
checks.evidence_quote: This patient was born with bilateral clubfoot, joint laxity, and dysmorphic facial features. At the age of 2 years she developed an aneurysmal brain hemorrhage.
checks.explanation: The abstract reports connective tissue and vascular features (joint laxity, aneurysmal hemorrhage) but does not mention skin fragility or easy bruising.

checks.claim: Heterozygous mutations in COL3A1 cause autosomal dominant vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: Mutations in the COL3A1 gene that encodes the chains of type III procollagen result in the vascular form of Ehlers-Danlos syndrome (EDS), EDS type IV, if they alter the sequence in the triple-helical domain.
checks.explanation: The abstract says COL3A1 mutations cause vascular EDS and calls them dominant mutations. The title's 'one COL3A1 allele' shows they are heterozygous.

paragraphs.text: Vandervore et al. (2017) reported patients from several unrelated families. They had a cobblestone-like cortical malformation, mainly frontal polymicrogyria-like overmigration, together with white matter abnormalities and cerebellar cysts. These brain findings resemble those in bilateral frontoparietal polymicrogyria caused by GPR56 mutations. Clinically, the patients had developmental delay and intellectual disability, and some had seizures. Some patients also had connective tissue findings consistent with Ehlers-Danlos syndrome.

checks.claim: Vandervore et al. (2017) reported patients with biallelic COL3A1-related disease from several unrelated families.
checks.evidence_quote: Brain imaging studies of this family and of two previously reported individuals with bi-allelic mutations in COL3A1 were reviewed.
checks.explanation: The paper reports one new family and reviews two previously reported individuals, three families in total. It does not report new patients from several unrelated families.

checks.claim: The patients reported by Vandervore et al. (2017) had a cobblestone-like cortical malformation, mainly frontal polymicrogyria-like overmigration.
checks.evidence_quote: Homozygous or compound heterozygous mutations in COL3A1 are associated with cobblestone-like malformation in all three families reported to date.
checks.explanation: The cobblestone-like malformation is stated. 'Mainly frontal polymicrogyria-like overmigration' is not in the abstract.

checks.claim: The patients reported by Vandervore et al. (2017) had white matter abnormalities.
checks.evidence_quote: Bi-allelic variants in COL3A1 encoding the ligand to GPR56 are associated with cobblestone-like cortical malformation, white matter changes and cerebellar cysts.
checks.explanation: The title states white matter changes.

checks.claim: The patients reported by Vandervore et al. (2017) had cerebellar cysts.
checks.evidence_quote: Bi-allelic variants in COL3A1 encoding the ligand to GPR56 are associated with cobblestone-like cortical malformation, white matter changes and cerebellar cysts.
checks.explanation: The title states cerebellar cysts.

checks.claim: The brain findings in the patients reported by Vandervore et al. (2017) resemble those in bilateral frontoparietal polymicrogyria caused by GPR56 mutations.
checks.evidence_quote: Brain MRI in the affected siblings as well as in the two previously reported individuals with bi-allelic COL3A1 mutations showed a brain phenotype similar to that associated with mutations in GPR56.
checks.explanation: The abstract states the resemblance to the GPR56 phenotype.

checks.claim: The patients reported by Vandervore et al. (2017) had developmental delay and intellectual disability.
checks.explanation: The abstract does not mention developmental delay or intellectual disability.

checks.claim: Some of the patients reported by Vandervore et al. (2017) had seizures.
checks.explanation: The abstract does not mention seizures.

checks.claim: Some of the patients reported by Vandervore et al. (2017) had connective tissue findings consistent with Ehlers-Danlos syndrome.
checks.explanation: The abstract does not mention connective tissue or EDS findings.

paragraphs.text: Horn et al. (2017) described patients with biallelic COL3A1 mutations. They showed a spectrum of specific structural brain anomalies, including polymicrogyria-type cortical malformation, combined with connective tissue abnormalities that overlapped with vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome.

checks.claim: Horn et al. (2017) described patients with biallelic COL3A1 mutations.
checks.evidence_quote: We identified biallelic COL3A1 variants in two unrelated families.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: The patients with biallelic COL3A1 mutations described by Horn et al. (2017) showed a spectrum of specific structural brain anomalies, including polymicrogyria-type cortical malformation.
checks.evidence_quote: Biallelic COL3A1 mutations result in a clinical spectrum of specific structural brain anomalies and connective tissue abnormalities.
checks.explanation: Polymicrogyria of the cobblestone variant is described.

checks.claim: The patients with biallelic COL3A1 mutations described by Horn et al. (2017) had connective tissue abnormalities overlapping with vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: Biallelic COL3A1 mutations result in a clinical spectrum of specific structural brain anomalies and connective tissue abnormalities.
checks.explanation: The connective tissue features (joint laxity, aneurysm, EDS phenotype) overlap with vascular EDS.

paragraphs.text: Autosomal recessive inheritance of this disorder was shown by the finding of homozygous or compound heterozygous COL3A1 mutations in affected individuals (Vandervore et al., 2017; Horn et al., 2017).

checks.claim: Polymicrogyria with or without vascular-type Ehlers-Danlos syndrome shows autosomal recessive inheritance, as shown by the finding of homozygous or compound heterozygous COL3A1 mutations in affected individuals.
checks.evidence_quote: Homozygous or compound heterozygous mutations in COL3A1 are associated with cobblestone-like malformation in all three families reported to date.
checks.explanation: Biallelic mutations in affected individuals support recessive inheritance.

paragraphs.text: Vandervore et al. (2017) identified biallelic COL3A1 mutations in patients with a cobblestone-like cortical malformation. They studied COL3A1 because collagen III is a ligand of GPR56 (ADGRG1), the receptor whose loss causes bilateral frontoparietal polymicrogyria.

checks.claim: Vandervore et al. (2017) identified biallelic COL3A1 mutations in patients with a cobblestone-like cortical malformation.
checks.evidence_quote: Homozygous or compound heterozygous mutations in COL3A1 are associated with cobblestone-like malformation in all three families reported to date.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: Vandervore et al. (2017) studied COL3A1 because collagen III is a ligand of GPR56 (ADGRG1).
checks.evidence_quote: Type III procollagen, the chains of which are encoded by COL3A1, is the ligand of the G protein-coupled receptor 56 (GPR56), also known as adhesion G protein-coupled receptor G1.
checks.explanation: The ligand relationship is stated. However, the variant was found by exome analysis, and the abstract does not say COL3A1 was studied because of the ligand relationship.

checks.claim: Loss of the receptor GPR56 (ADGRG1) causes bilateral frontoparietal polymicrogyria.
checks.evidence_quote: Bi-allelic mutations in GPR56 give rise to cobblestone-like malformation, white matter changes and cerebellar dysplasia.
checks.explanation: The abstract describes the GPR56 phenotype as a cobblestone-like malformation. It does not name it bilateral frontoparietal polymicrogyria.

paragraphs.text: Horn et al. (2017) reported more patients with biallelic COL3A1 mutations and a combination of brain malformations and connective tissue abnormalities.

checks.claim: Horn et al. (2017) reported additional patients with biallelic COL3A1 mutations.
checks.evidence_quote: We identified biallelic COL3A1 variants in two unrelated families.
checks.explanation: The abstract reports new families, in addition to three previously reported ones.

checks.claim: The patients with biallelic COL3A1 mutations reported by Horn et al. (2017) had a combination of brain malformations and connective tissue abnormalities.
checks.evidence_quote: Biallelic COL3A1 mutations result in a clinical spectrum of specific structural brain anomalies and connective tissue abnormalities.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

paragraphs.text: Luo et al. (2011) identified collagen III as the ligand of GPR56 in the developing brain. Col3a1-null mice had cortical malformations, with neurons migrating past the pial basement membrane, which resembled the cobblestone-like defect seen in Gpr56-deficient mice.

checks.claim: Luo et al. (2011) identified collagen III as the ligand of GPR56 in the developing brain.
checks.evidence_quote: Recently, we discovered that collagen III is the ligand of GPR56 [15].
checks.explanation: The paper calls collagen III the GPR56 ligand and says it is in the pial BM, citing the authors' earlier work. It does not name Luo et al. (2011) in the supplied text, so the attribution to them cannot be confirmed here.

checks.claim: Col3a1-null mice had cortical malformations in which neurons migrated past the pial basement membrane.
checks.evidence_quote: Regional breakdown of the pial BM with concurrent neuronal overmigration was observed in about half of the E11.5 and all embryos older than E12.5 in the Col3a1 −/− brains analyzed
checks.explanation: The paper reports pial BM breakdown in Col3a1-null brains, with neurons overmigrating through it into ectopias.

checks.claim: The cortical malformation in Col3a1-null mice resembled the cobblestone-like defect seen in Gpr56-deficient mice.
checks.evidence_quote: suggesting that the ectopic cells in the Col3a1 −/− cortex were neurons from both deep and superficial cortical layers, mirroring our observations of Gpr56 null mutant mice
checks.explanation: The paper describes a cobblestone-like cortical malformation and says it mirrors what was seen in Gpr56-null mice.
